title: Burst Balloons
pattern: Interval DP: choose the balloon that is burst last
statement: Each balloon has a number. Bursting balloon `i` earns `nums[i − 1] · nums[i] · nums[i + 1]` coins, where the neighbours are the nearest balloons still **unburst** (a missing neighbour counts as 1). Burst all balloons; return the maximum number of coins.
idea: Choosing which balloon to burst **first** is messy: its two neighbours become adjacent, so the remaining parts influence each other.

Think backwards — choose which balloon in an interval is burst **last**. When it finally bursts, everything else between the interval's two borders is already gone, so its neighbours are exactly those two borders. And the parts to its left and right were solved independently.

`dp[left][right]` = best coins from bursting everything **strictly between** `left` and `right`. Try every `k` in between as the last balloon: `nums[left]·nums[k]·nums[right] + dp[left][k] + dp[k][right]`. Solve short intervals first.

complexity.timeWhy: O(n²) intervals, and up to n choices for the last balloon in each.
complexity.spaceWhy: The table has one cell for every pair (left, right).

steps.text: Our example: **`nums = [3,1,5]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
